name: Corporate statism
summary: Corporate statism organises society into officially designated functional groups, usually by economic sector, that the state recognises, controls and incorporates into policymaking. It replaces class conflict and party competition with state-arbitrated cooperation among employers, workers and other interests, within a strong, authoritarian state. Private ownership usually survives, under heavy state direction of investment, wages and prices.
scope: The authoritarian state-corporatist strand as practised in Mussolini's Italy (1922-1943), Salazar's Estado Novo in Portugal, and the interwar Austrian Federal State, with Othmar Spann's theory and Catholic social teaching (Quadragesimo Anno) as intellectual sources. It excludes democratic neo-corporatism or social partnership and corporate nationalism, which works through private corporations. Many non-economic questions are inferred from the regimes' Catholic-traditionalist and nationalist character, and Fascist Italy differed from Portugal on war, race and the leader cult.

keyFigures.name: Benito Mussolini
keyFigures.role: Leader of Fascist Italy, whose corporate state is the best-known example

keyFigures.name: António de Oliveira Salazar
keyFigures.role: Architect of Portugal's corporatist 1933 constitution and ruler of the Estado Novo

keyFigures.name: Othmar Spann
keyFigures.role: Austrian theorist whose universalist ideas are linked to corporate statism

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were set by state-supervised collective contracts between recognised bodies, not by a statutory floor, and adherents leaned towards restraint rather than substantial rises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Corporatists hold that free competition cannot direct economic life and must be coordinated by state-recognised bodies, though private enterprise is retained.

public-ownership.rationale: The Estado Novo kept a mixed economy with private ownership under heavy state regulation, so wholesale public ownership was not the model.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Corporate statist regimes harnessed capitalists as partners and did not campaign on soaking the rich; no clear doctrine, so split.

unions-good.rationale: Free unions were replaced by state-controlled official syndicates, so independent unions are rejected even though state-run syndicates are central.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property is kept, but with a social function and state limits for the common good, so adherents neither treat it as inviolable nor reject it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state has broad authority over investment, wages and prices, and economic actors are subordinated to the national interest.

cut-welfare.rationale: Regimes offered welfare to syndicalised workers to win loyalty; cutting it runs against the bargain, though welfare was not expansive.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers are organised into syndicates beside employers rather than owning firms; Quadragesimo Anno advises that workers may share in ownership, management or profits through partnership contracts, but not collective ownership.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addressed; these regimes restricted speech widely but for political reasons, not on hate-speech grounds.

strong-leader.rationale: The Estado Novo article says the president was on paper a virtual dictator and that his power to dismiss Salazar was the only check on Salazar's power under an anti-parliamentarian constitution.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is the organising centre of society; the Fascist formula was everything within the state, nothing outside it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Order-based regimes emerging from the 1926 coup relied on police and military backing and suppressed opposition.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: Corporate statism is centralised, with sectoral bodies recognised and controlled by the national state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not central to the doctrine; regimes mixed harsh repression with rhetoric of order.

traditional-family.rationale: The Estado Novo motto was God, Fatherland and Family, and labour associations were framed as natural orders like the family.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Estado Novo drew on Catholic social doctrine, with the Church privileged, though Fascist Italy was more ambivalent.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nation-first traditionalism, as in God, Fatherland and Family, makes cultural preservation central.

gradual-change.rationale: The regimes broke with liberal parliamentary institutions yet claimed to preserve a natural social order; adherents are split.

free-trade.rationale: The Estado Novo ran strong protectionism and corporatist regimes favoured managed national economies.

nation-first.rationale: Nation-centred, with Portugal's pluricontinental nation and Italian nationalism as pillars.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: Corporatists present themselves as ending class conflict and preserving order, rejecting revolution from below, though Fascism came to power by force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Policy is made through designated functional bodies and the state rather than mass electoral politics.

central-planning.rationale: These regimes directed investment and wages but kept private ownership, not comprehensive central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership by workers or the public is not the corporatist model of private owners and workers cooperating under the state.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare was tied to syndicate membership and work, not unconditional.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Estado Novo was strongly protectionist and corporate states favoured managed national economies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Estado Novo article states that the state exercised extensive authority over private investment decisions and the level of wages.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno favours wide ownership but the regimes protected large business too; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno rejects the view that the wage contract is unjust in itself and demands a wage sufficient to support a worker and his family.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Strong state economic control is inconsistent with abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The defining feature: citizens organised into state-recognised bodies, with the state as final arbiter of wages and conditions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Italy and Portugal ran single-party states, though corporate statism is more about a ruling party mediating; the Estado Novo party was a support structure and not ideologically driven.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Regimes varied (Italy kept a king, Portugal a republic, Austria Catholic authoritarian); no uniform stance.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1933 constitution set up an anti-parliamentarian and authoritarian government and restricted the legislature to members of the National Union.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscites were used for legitimacy as in 1933, but direct legislative votes were not a principle.

right-to-secede.rationale: Portugal treated its colonies as extensions of the nation and centralised states reject secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hierarchical order and strong leadership mean adherents accept that some are suited to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Regimes used violence and a secret police against opponents and claimed rule by force.

separate-church-state.rationale: The regimes allied with the Church and Catholic social doctrine, not strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural-law inspiration is influential but laws were not framed on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Corporate statism makes the state the organising centre of society, so handing courts, policing and defense to private firms contradicts its premise.

military-superiority.rationale: Strong state power and nationalism lead to a preference for strength, though small Portugal was less ambitious.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Italy and Portugal's corporatism is not primarily ethnic; Austrian and Italian versions differ.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno criticises the huge gap between rich and propertyless, but the system keeps owners and wage earners in distinct, harmonised orders rather than seeking equal outcomes.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Regimes defended their empires as civilising projects.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Corporatism subordinates individual economic interest to social function and the national interest.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Order and continuity matter more than disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Catholic corporatists appeal to a medieval guild order, while Fascists claimed novelty; split.

direct-action.rationale: The state controls political activity, and independent direct action is repressed.

production-for-use.rationale: Production stays for profit in private firms, subordinated to national goals.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno denies that the wage contract is unjust in itself and calls for capital and labour to cooperate, rejecting the exploitation thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Corporatism offers class collaboration as the alternative to Marxist class rule, and Quadragesimo Anno condemns communism's class warfare.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Corporatists reject Marxist claims and see capitalism reformable by organisation.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is central and taxation legitimate.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Estado Novo was in theory a corporatist state representing interest groups rather than individuals, implying groups hold standing of their own.

media-academia-power.rationale: Regimes controlled media directly; the claim itself is not a doctrinal one.

organic-representation.rationale: The Estado Novo's Corporative Chamber seated municipalities and religious, cultural and professional groups as a state representing interest groups rather than individuals; representation through families comes from the Catholic model.

total-state.rationale: The Fascist formula is total statism, but other corporatist cases, such as Portugal, were more limited; the state was dominant in the economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Regimes presented themselves as national regeneration after instability.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Italy expanded; Portugal sought only to hold its empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a state, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Corporate states replaced guild and landlord ties with state-recognised workers' syndicates and wage contracts, not legal bondage to land.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic natural law underpins the Catholic strand.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Corporate statism does not address Zionism, and its historical regimes held varied views; no basis for a lean.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a corporatist concern and the regimes did not share a policy on it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Representation is through state-recognised sectoral bodies, not worker votes in firms.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Salazar was famed for balanced budgets; Italy was not so; contested.

economic-freedom.rationale: Free competition is distrusted, and political freedom was not tied to economic freedom.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalist, yet colonial regimes denied it to others.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not a corporatist stance; the Catholic strand privileges faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits were attached to national syndicate membership.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare was linked to employment through syndicates.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Corporatism article says the 1927 Labour Charter became the main form of class collaboration in the Fascist government, and Quadragesimo Anno urges cooperation in place of class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Regimes built on God, Fatherland and Family valued inherited institutions and tradition and would not sacrifice them to novelty.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers are organised nationally under the state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Estado Novo's family-centred ideology and its stricter voting rules for women reflect a distinct public role for the sexes.

ban-interest.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno does not call for a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not Salazarist doctrine; Fascist Italy imposed it late; core view is no.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Corporate statism article describes the ruling party acting as a mediator between workers, capitalists and other major state interests, not as a class's tool.

proportional-representation.rationale: Corporate statism replaces party representation with representation through officially designated functional groups.

national-mission.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale describes a mission that is not about spreading a form of government (religious, cultural, racial, imperial or leadership), and the statement now asks whether the country should treat spreading its form of government abroad as a special national mission.

reviewHistory.rationale: Italy and Portugal had civilising mission rhetoric.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Regimes attacked parliamentary politicians but stressed their own virtue.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic regimes rejected eugenics generally; contested.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Estado Novo's secret police PIDE persecuted opponents and was shielded from accountability under the regime.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Estado Novo state exercised extensive authority over private investment decisions and the level of wages, far beyond defence, justice and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic belief in equal dignity but legal hierarchies by function and nation; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Corporatism rejects socialism as such; Quadragesimo Anno says Christian socialism is a contradiction in terms.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Estado Novo treated overseas territories as extensions of Portugal and encouraged settlement, rejecting a colonial framing.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; corporate statists hold no stake, though a strong state is congenial to them.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rests on the state, with plebiscites ritual.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Corporate states exercise state coercion and suppressed opposition, so adherents reject a rule against initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Free competition destroys itself; cooperation preferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Single-party regimes banned rivals; the Estado Novo allowed only the National Union party and tightly controlled opposition.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in the executive, as under Salazar, with a limited National Assembly.

vanguard-party.rationale: Corporatism rejects Marxist revolution and class politics; a revolutionary vanguard party is the opposite of class collaboration.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching stresses the poor but corporatism stresses function.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A policy of a late-twentieth-century democracy and not a corporatist question.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the new syndical order as forbidding strikes and lock-outs, with the State intervening when the parties cannot settle a dispute.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Corporate statism relies on appointed and group-designated authority, not random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian corporate regimes tightly controlled opposition and ruled by emergency-style powers against enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state held broad authority over wages and prices in the corporate system.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalist and sovereignty-focused regimes resisted supranational pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president or leader held executive control, with Salazar holding effective control of government in Portugal.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Catholic-aligned regimes supported the hierarchical Church; adherents of other confessions would differ, so low.

clerical-rule.rationale: Salazar rejected clerical rule even though Catholic.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Corporatism seeks national solidarity across classes and condemns the class war on which revolutionary defeatism depends.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Estado Novo's presidents stood repeatedly and Salazar ruled for decades with no electoral check.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority flows from the top down; recalling officials by voters contradicts the anti-parliamentary design.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Portugal held NATO membership and the Anglo-Portuguese alliance.

people-in-arms.rationale: Standing forces; Fascist militias were party arms.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Regimes justified their empires by civilising claims such as lusotropicalism, implying hierarchy among societies.

death-penalty.rationale: Salazar abolished it; Italy reinstated; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Citizens are fitted into designated groups with considerable group control over members, leaving little room for eccentricity.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1933 constitution was imposed by a plebiscite engineered by Salazar, not drawn up by an elected assembly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mixed; Portugal's president popularly elected nominally.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state held broad authority over investment and economic policy, so an independent bank is at odds with it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says ownership has an individual and a social character, owners must consider the common good, and the State may define the duties of ownership.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Estado Novo was closely allied with the Catholic Church and drew on its social doctrine rather than curbing it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Estado Novo held its overseas territories as part of a single nation and fought to keep them; centralised states resist secession.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Split: leaders held dominant authority but regimes issued constitutions and claimed legality.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of leader was a feature in Italy; Salazar was less showy.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Corporatism rejects the premise of class struggle and of socialism itself.

land-redistribution.rationale: Landowners remained part of the corporate order; redistribution contradicts the mixed, private-ownership economy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Split: Fascist Italy pursued irredentist claims while the Estado Novo did not.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno rejects the Marxist account of history and a purely materialist view of society.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporate statism replaces market competition with government-directed sector bodies; Quadragesimo Anno attacks concentrated economic power but holds that free competition cannot direct economic life, so protecting competition is not the aim.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Strong protectionism in the Estado Novo and autarky in Fascist Italy fit this, though it was not universal.

moral-incentives.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno stresses duties and social charity but corporate regimes still used wages and profit.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchy and social orders were preserved and not levelled by corporate states.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Estado Novo justified empire by lusotropicalism and civilising claims.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Corporatism claims that organised cooperation and reform can avoid collapse of capitalism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Authoritarian state-corporatist regimes rejected liberal constitutional limits and gave the state primacy over individual rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Portugal and Italy held colonial empires as national missions and defended their borders, so imposed treaties are not set aside.

minority-veto.rationale: The corporative state makes the common good, as defined by the state, binding on all groups, leaving no individual veto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Estado Novo and Fascist Italy were anti-parliamentarist and replaced party-based parliaments with corporative chambers.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds that owners must use surplus wealth for the common good and charity, and class collaboration rests on mutual duties.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Fascist Italy used 'proletarian nation' claims against richer powers, but Portugal did not; adherents are split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued autarky and Estado Novo ran a protectionist economy aimed at national self-sufficiency.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The corporative regimes were founded in opposition to liberalism, socialism and antifascism, and banned antifascist parties.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents condemn communism but defended their own regimes, and Salazar rejected the totalitarian label for the Estado Novo.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The regimes explicitly rejected liberal democracy in favour of corporative forms they thought suited their nations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Estado Novo arose from the 1926 military coup and the army remained its pillar; Fascist Italy also treated the armed forces as guardians of the state.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Fascist Italy had no divorce and the Estado Novo restricted it for Catholic marriages, so adherents oppose easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The state recognises and controls representation by sector and replaces party competition; binding and recalling delegates runs against that.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Corporatist states subordinated parliament to the executive and the corporative chambers; budget control by an elected parliament was weakened.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Italy backed foreign movements for its aims while Portugal stayed cautious; adherents split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The authoritarian state demands obedience, and the Estado Novo constitution placed the state above individuals and parties.

non-intervention.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued interventionist wars while Salazar's Portugal stayed neutral, so adherents were split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Compulsory syndicates were organised by economic sector, with workers and employers together in each branch.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno and the Estado Novo defended marriage and the family as basic institutions under church and state.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Estado Novo ran censorship and a political police, so state secrecy was the norm.

informal-organisation.rationale: The system required officially recognised formal bodies for every sector and banned independent organising.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: Private property in the means of production survives, defended by Quadragesimo Anno and the regimes.

defeat-communism.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns socialism and the Estado Novo and Fascist Italy were anti-communist.

religion-illusion.rationale: Catholic-traditionalist regimes upheld religion as true and socially necessary.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno criticises liberal free competition and capital concentration, and corporatism is offered as the alternative.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Corporate statism puts groups under state control rather than self-governing communities holding common property.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corporatism was presented as a third path between liberal capitalism and socialism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Corporate statism replaces party competition and class conflict with state-controlled groups within an authoritarian state.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Italy and Portugal held overseas empires and governed them in the interest of the metropole.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Decisions go through state-recognised functional groups under an authoritarian state, not direct popular participation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: These are authoritarian, nationalist regimes that built and valued strong armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Portugal stayed neutral in WWII while Fascist Italy joined the Axis, so the strands split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Corporate states kept private banking under state direction, and Quadragesimo Anno criticised finance power but did not call for user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The regimes favoured national self-sufficiency but Salazar also stressed balanced budgets; no clear position.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Corporatism replaces popular and party politics with state-recognised functional bodies and an authoritarian state, so decision by lay citizens chosen by lot runs against its core design.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns the concentration of economic power in a few hands as a despotic dictatorship, and corporatism aimed to subordinate capital to the state; its remedy is state direction, not liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The regimes were Catholic-aligned (Lateran accords, Estado Novo's Church ties) and none promoted atheism through schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A strong authoritarian state with a powerful police apparatus is central to the model, so abolition is rejected.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fascist Italy and the Estado Novo ran state youth organisations (Balilla, Mocidade Portuguesa) to train youth for the nation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Catholic teaching and the regimes accepted lethal force for defence of person and state.

independent-unions.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the Italian corporative system as replacing free unions with state-recognised syndicates, and Estado Novo likewise bound unions to the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Corporate statism rejects class struggle and working-class rule in favour of state arbitration among sectors.

second-chamber.rationale: Corporate systems typically replaced or complemented elected chambers with a chamber of corporations, as in Portugal's Corporative Chamber and Fascist Italy's Chamber of Fasces and Corporations.

municipal-property.rationale: Private ownership survives under state direction, and the state, not the locality, sits at the centre; local collective ownership is not part of the system.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The system is a top-down authoritarian state, so decisions rest with the state, not local assemblies coordinated by delegates.

family-wage.rationale: Catholic social teaching in Quadragesimo Anno holds that wages should be enough to support a worker and his family, and Estado Novo promoted the male-breadwinner household.

person-over-state.rationale: Corporate statism subordinates individuals to the state and the functional groups; Quadragesimo Anno stresses human dignity but the regimes treated the person as serving the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno and the Catholic-traditionalist regimes, notably Salazar's, held that society should serve spiritual as well as material ends.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Authoritarian unitary states held all regional and local power at the centre's discretion, as in Salazar's centralised Portugal.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fascist Italy used linguistic irredentism while Salazar's Portugal and Austria's Federal State did not; the strands split.

capital-controls.rationale: The state directed investment and the economy, and Italy and Portugal ran autarkic policies with controls on capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Strong authoritarian corporatist states claimed a monopoly of force, disbanding rival armed groups or absorbing them into the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Fascist Italy and the Estado Novo demanded discipline and obedience from soldiers; refusal would be treason.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wages were set through state-sanctioned corporations or compulsory arbitration, not free bargaining by independent unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The regimes had state-run welfare and family allowances but no documented tax-credit tradition; adherents are split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The system imposes a state-defined blueprint of sectoral corporations rather than letting communities choose economic systems.

sacred-nation.rationale: The regimes and their Catholic-traditionalist and nationalist outlook treated the nation as an organic community above individuals.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Catholic social teaching, a source of corporatism, grounds dignity in a fixed human nature; Fascist Italy's view differed.

public-service-media.rationale: The regimes controlled the press and broadcasting for state purposes, not independent public media.

workers-own-party.rationale: Corporate statism replaces class conflict and party competition with officially designated sectoral bodies, leaving no place for an independent workers' party.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Syndicates were state-recognised and membership dues were levied on all workers in the sector, so union membership was effectively compulsory.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Catholic traditionalist regimes (Italy after the Lateran Pacts, Estado Novo, Austria) gave the Catholic Church a privileged legal position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: It replaces party competition with state-arbitrated cooperation among functional groups, so competitive elections do not define legitimate government.

race-social-construct.rationale: Adherents split: Fascist Italy adopted racial laws in 1938 while Portugal and Austria did not make race central.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Catholic corporatists and secular Fascists differed on the place of scripture; adherents are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Corporatist systems built higher chambers from delegates of the occupational bodies rather than direct popular votes.

national-church-status.rationale: The Estado Novo and the Austrian state were Catholic-corporatist and gave the Church a privileged place, following Quadragesimo Anno.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Parties were abolished or subordinated, but interest groups were deliberately incorporated as state-recognised bodies, so adherents agree on one half and not the other.

national-resource-control.rationale: Italy and Portugal pursued protectionist, state-directed economies with national control of key sectors and colonial resources.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Catholic-corporatist adherents lean on natural law while the Fascist state treated law as the state's will, so adherents are split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds that capital and labour need each other in production, rejecting labour as the sole source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The corporate state binds class collaboration to national unity, presenting service to the nation as service to its producers.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Private ownership under an authoritarian state is accepted, but Quadragesimo Anno rejects socialism and communist leadership; the statement's socialist framing is rejected.

police-more-powers.rationale: Order-based regimes emerging from the 1926 coup relied on police and military backing and suppressed opposition. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Regimes offered welfare to syndicalised workers to win loyalty; cutting it runs against the bargain, though welfare was not expansive. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Strikes and lock-outs should be forbidden, with disputes between employers and workers settled by a public authority.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the Italian corporative system as forbidding strikes and lock-outs and sending unresolved disputes to state arbitration, and the Fascist system made the state final arbiter.

missingStatements.text: Every worker and employer should be required to belong to one officially recognised body for their sector.
missingStatements.rationale: Corporate statism requires citizens to belong to officially designated interest groups, usually by economic sector.

notes: Fascist Italy, Salazar's Portugal and Catholic corporatists differ: Italy was more totalitarian, militarist and expansionist, Portugal more conservative and Church-aligned, and Quadragesimo Anno voices reservations about state-run syndicates. Many answers on social and foreign policy are low-confidence inferences.
